integrity: The global rigidity uses the proved nondecreasing theorem, real analyticity of positive-exponent moments, the source exponent-derivative identity, and the independently published equality classification for the homogeneous entropy inequality. The quantitative defect is reconstructed from the source area identity and positive kernel, Harnack's inequality, and an exact weighted Dirichlet coefficient integral. No numerical sampling or finite enumeration is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The global equality classification applies to arbitrary multiplicities, but the explicit derivative defect is proved only on the simple-root stratum where the source polar factor is zero-free on the closed disk. The defect is not claimed to have the optimal numerical coefficient and is not converted into an angular zero-discrepancy estimate.
title: Equality rigidity and a quantitative defect for Baernstein monotonicity
